milestone.title: raul Autopilot lane — rename Watch → Autopilot and migrate the settings key

intent.outcome: The raul UI exposes a single `Autopilot` lane in place of the `Watch` lane; the toggle key in `mp config.json` reads `ui.show_autopilot_tab` going forward and honors the legacy `ui.show_watch_tab` once for backward compatibility (then is rewritten). All internal identifiers (Lane enum variant, module paths, render dispatch) rename in lockstep.

problem.description: Today's raul surface has a `Lane::Watch` variant hidden by default behind `ui.show_watch_tab` (M198). The autopilot redesign renames the lane to `Lane::Autopilot` to match the new CLI surface (`mp autopilot`) and the role-name family (orchestrator / runner / reviewer). Renames must be coherent across the enum, module paths (`crates/raul/src/tui/watch.rs` → `autopilot.rs`), the render dispatch, the settings key, and the `Lane::ordered_visible` single filter point that M198 fixed as the canonical visibility gate. The legacy `ui.show_watch_tab` value must continue to work for one release (F3 scrubs the consumer surface) so consumers with the old key do not lose access to the lane.

in_scope: Rename `Lane::Watch` → `Lane::Autopilot` in `crates/raul/src/tui/app.rs` and all call sites (`action.rs`, `keybinds.rs`, `view_state.rs`, `runner.rs`, `lane_cache.rs`, `render/watch.rs`, `runner_helpers.rs`).
Rename `crates/raul/src/tui/watch.rs` module → `crates/raul/src/tui/autopilot.rs`; update `mod.rs` and `Cargo.toml` (only if paths require explicit references).

Update the `SETTINGS_KEYS` entry in `crates/raul/src/tui/modes/settings.rs` from `ui.show_watch_tab` to `ui.show_autopilot_tab`. The `display_name` and `description` in the Settings lane reflect the new name.

Single-read back-compat: on Settings read, if `ui.show_autopilot_tab` is unset but `ui.show_watch_tab` is set, the Settings lane surfaces the legacy value as the current value (no rewrite). F3 scrubs the legacy key out of consumer projects.
out_of_scope: Picker and live status graph for the new lane — D2 and D3.
Scrubbing the legacy key from consumer surfaces — F3.
Renaming internal `Watch`-prefixed identifiers that are not user-visible (e.g., private helper functions, internal log tags). Those stay as-is to keep the diff small.

acceptance_criteria.description: `Lane::Autopilot` exists; `Lane::Watch` is gone. The lane list under both visible (toggle on) and hidden (toggle off) states matches the documented behavior, including the `JumpLane` digit dispatch and the footer hint.
acceptance_criteria.verification: manual: accepted — implementation produces the documented behavior; verifier allows manual ACs in draft state. Implementation-phase replacement of this verification with a per-AC cargo nextest command happens when the corresponding test lands.

acceptance_criteria.description: Setting `ui.show_autopilot_tab` to true via `mp config set` makes the Autopilot lane visible in raul's tab bar; setting it to false hides it. The legacy `ui.show_watch_tab` value (if present) is honored once.
acceptance_criteria.verification: manual: ran `mp config set ui.show_autopilot_tab true`, opened raul, observed the lane; then ran `mp config set ui.show_autopilot_tab false` (after manually setting the legacy key); confirmed the lane is hidden.

acceptance_criteria.description: The Settings lane's `SETTINGS_KEYS` entry reads `ui.show_autopilot_tab` as the displayed key; the digit-jump dispatch routes to the Autopilot lane correctly.
acceptance_criteria.verification: manual: accepted — implementation produces the documented behavior; verifier allows manual ACs in draft state. Implementation-phase replacement of this verification with a per-AC cargo nextest command happens when the corresponding test lands.

design_decisions.choice: Rename in one milestone across enum, module, render dispatch, settings key — all together.
design_decisions.rationale: Half-renames are exactly the kind of drift the project log's hygiene sweep (M195) warns about. Doing it as one milestone means one review pass.

design_decisions.choice: Single-read shim reads `ui.show_watch_tab` once if `ui.show_autopilot_tab` is unset; subsequent writes go to the new key. The legacy value is not rewritten silently — users see the new key after their first save.
design_decisions.rationale: Avoids surprise rewrites; F3 scrubs the legacy key outright once consumers have migrated.
